nodes.name: Anodic electrodeposition on ITO
nodes.procedure: Controlled-potential electrolysis (CPE) was applied to form the surface-bound NiFeOx catalyst in 2 M Na2CO3 (pH 10.8) at 1.3 V vs NHE for 15 min in the presence of 1 mM Ni(II) and 1 mM Fe(III). The catalytic current density increases rapidly from 0.2 to 14 mA/cm^2 in only 15 min and is sustained.
nodes.source_text: CPE was applied to form the surface-bound NiFeOx catalyst in 2MNa2CO3 (pH10.8) at 1.3V (Figure 1B). In the presence of 1mM Ni(II) and 1mMFe(III), the catalytic current density increases rapidly from 0.2 to 14mA/cm^2 in only 15min

nodes.name: Rapid anodic electrodeposition on ITO with Fe(II)
nodes.procedure: Controlled-potential electrolysis (CPE) at 1.3 V vs NHE in 2 M Na2CO3 (pH 10.8) solution containing 0.6 mM Ni(II) and 1.4 mM Fe(II) for 3 min on ITO electrode under strict O2-free conditions with N2 flow.
nodes.source_text: electrolysis with Ni(II) and Fe(II) results in an even faster current increase, reaching a saturated current density in only 3min (Figure 4A)... with 0.6mM Ni(II) and 1.4mM Fe(II)

nodes.name: Anodic electrodeposition on nickel foam
nodes.procedure: Controlled-potential electrolysis (CPE) at 1.3 V vs NHE in 2 M Na2CO3 (pH 10.8) solution with 1 mM Ni(II) and 1 mM Fe(III) for 15 min on nickel foam (NF) electrode. Current density increased from 50 to 320 mA/cm^2 in 3 min and leveled off in 15 min.
nodes.source_text: electrolysis in 2MNa2CO3 (pH10.8) solution with 1mM Ni(II) and 1mM Fe(III) resulted in a rapid increase in current density which increased from 50 to 320mA/cm^2 in 3min and gradually leveled off in 15min (Figure 5A)

nodes.description: OER performance in 2 M Na₂CO₃ (pH 10.8) and 1 M KOH
nodes.source_text: The Tafel slope ... 40 mV/decade was obtained in 2 M Na₂CO₃ (pH 10.8) solution. The same measurement was conducted in 1 M KOH, and a smaller Tafel slope of 28 mV/decade was achieved ... a current density of 10 mA/cm² was achieved with an overpotential of 310 mV in 1 M KOH

nodes.description: OER stability CPE in 2 M Na₂CO₃ at fixed potentials
nodes.source_text: CPE experiments with the catalyst film ... were conducted in 2 M Na₂CO₃ (pH 10.8) at 1.0, 1.1, and 1.2 V, respectively. ... sustained catalytic currents were achieved at all applied potentials for at least 10 h. ... the film prepared by 15 min of CPE is equivalent to those of 30 and 60 min

nodes.description: OER LSV in 1 M KOH with iR compensation
nodes.source_text: the OER process ... exhibits a catalytic onset potential of 0.64 V in 1 M KOH. ... a current density of 100 mA/cm² is obtained at an overpotential of 260 mV. The Tafel slope ... is 28 mV/decade ... At the final step, a current density of 500 mA/cm² was obtained at a potential of 0.87 V, which corresponds to an overpotential of only 440 mV

nodes.description: Long-term CPE stability in 1 M KOH at 0.75 V
nodes.source_text: the catalytic current gradually decreases from 150 to 90 mA/cm² during 40 h of electrolysis in 1 M KOH at 0.75 V, which corresponds to a decrease of 1%/h

nodes.description: Enhanced stability CPE with self-repair additives
nodes.source_text: In a solution mixture of 1 M KOH and 2 M Na₂CO₃ (red line), the catalytic current decreases from 152 to 132 mA/cm², corresponding to a decrease of 0.33%/h

multistep chronopotentiometric curve ... current was increased from 50 to 500 mA/cm² with an increment of 50 mA/cm² per 600 s ... At the start of 50 mA/cm², the potential immediately levels off at 0.71 V ... at the final step ... 500 mA/cm² was obtained at a potential of 0.87 V
the turnover frequency (TOF) of the FeNiOₓ film by 15 min of CPE was 0.68 s⁻¹ per deposited metal ion at an overpotential of 310 mV

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM of NiFeOx catalyst scraped from ITO electrode exhibited layered structures.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) of the material scraped from the ITO electrode exhibited layered structures (Figure S12A,B in the Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows no lattice fringes indicating poor crystallinity of the deposited NiFeOx material.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The observation of no lattice in the high-resolution TEM (HRTEM) image (Figure S12C) and the poorly defined diffraction rings in the selected area electron diffraction (SAED) pattern (Figure S12A, insert) indicated the poor crystallinity of the deposited material on the electrode.

nodes.characterization_summary: SAED pattern shows poorly defined diffraction rings confirming poor crystallinity of NiFeOx.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The observation of no lattice in the high-resolution TEM (HRTEM) image (Figure S12C) and the poorly defined diffraction rings in the selected area electron diffraction (SAED) pattern (Figure S12A, insert) indicated the poor crystallinity of the deposited material on the electrode.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD pattern shows broad amorphous features with no peaks indicative of crystalline phases other than ITO.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Xray diffraction (XRD) pattern of the electrodeposited catalyst film (Figure S13 in the Supporting Information) includes broad amorphous features and no peaks indicative of crystalline phases other than the peaks associated with the ITO layer.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDX shows uniform distribution of Ni, Fe, and O with Ni:Fe molar ratio of 0.53:0.47.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The energy-dispersive X-ray (EDX) results in Figure S14 in the Supporting Information show that the amorphous solid was a mixture containing Ni, Fe, and O, which are distributed uniformly on the electrode substrate. The quantitative analysis shows a Ni:Fe molar ratio of 0.53:0.47 in this optimized film.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni 2p XPS peaks at 855.7 and 873.3 eV characteristic of Ni(II); Fe 2p binding energies indicate Fe(III) valence state in amorphous NiFeOx catalyst.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Ni 2p spectrum displays two dominant peaks at 855.7 and 873.3 eV... characteristic of Ni(II).[26] ... The binding energies of Fe 2p of the electrodeposited catalyst film suggest that the valence state of Fe is Fe(III).

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-OES analysis shows 20 nmol/cm² Ni and 18 nmol/cm² Fe, corresponding to 30 Ni and 27 Fe atoms per 25Å².
nodes.evidence_snippet: The number of deposited Ni and Fe atoms could be determined by dissolving the catalyst film in 0.1M HNO3 followed by analysis by inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectroscopy (ICP-OES). ... 18 nmol of iron and 20 nmol of nickel were electrodeposited onto the ITO electrode per square centimeter, which corresponds to 27 Fe atoms and 30 Ni atoms per 25Å².

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM of NiFeOx/NF shows grasslike structures with diameter ~30 nm and length ~200 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The inset in Figure 5B displays a high-resolution SEM image of the NiFeOx/NF surface as marked. The NiFeOx deposits consist of grasslike structures with a diameter of ~30 nm and a length of ~200 nm growing from the nanoparticle layer.

nodes.characterization_summary: AFM measurement shows catalyst film thickness of around 30 nm for 60 min CPE.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The AFM measurement shows that the thickness of the catalyst film by 60 min of CPE is around 30 nm (Figure S10 in the Supporting Information).
